D003.notes: Specifies standard Lebesgue measure and absolute integrability. The totalized integral convention explicitly supplies no finiteness, so integrability remains an exported proof obligation.

D004.notes: Ω is precisely the open positive-time domain. Ordinary local derivatives there require no extension regularity or conclusion at time zero.

D005.notes: The piecewise extension exists for every supplied u and q, agrees with u on Ω, and asserts no regularity across t=0. Positive-time germs are unchanged.

D006.notes: Directional derivative is evaluation of the Fréchet derivative, with the explicit zero convention when differentiation fails. This defines notation without granting differentiability.

D007.notes: The standard basis exists canonically in ℝ^n. Changing 1,…,n to Fin n only relabels orthonormal coordinates and preserves the Euclidean measure.

D008.notes: T=(0,1) is a defined constant vector in Xn×ℝ; no hypothesis or existence condition is hidden.

D009.notes: S_j=(b_j,0) is defined for each finite spatial coordinate using D007; its type and dependence on n are explicit.

D010.notes: All first and iterated derivatives are specified in constant directions on Ω. Arbitrary extensions agree on neighborhoods of positive-time points, so the derivative germs are well defined there. The componentwise Laplacian and Frobenius square match the original normalization.

D011.notes: The energy density is exactly |u_t|²+Σ_j|∂_{x_j}u|², without a factor 1/2. Zero extension outside positive time asserts no integrability or regularity.

D012.notes: The scalar flux is explicitly ⟨u_t,∂_{x_j}u⟩ for j=1,…,n. Its definition grants neither smoothness nor support; those are internal conclusions.

D013.notes: The energy is the Lebesgue integral of D011 at each positive time; integrability and differentiability are explicitly not assumed. The total extension has the same positive-time restriction.

D014.notes: Topological support means the closure of the nonzero set in the stated domain. This defines compact support without assuming any particular function has it.
